original_question: Which isoform of the gene associated with Paroxysmal Nonkinesigenic Dyskinesia is predominantly expressed in the central nervous system?

final_qi.question: Which isoform of the gene associated with Paroxysmal Nonkinesigenic Dyskinesia is predominantly expressed in the central nervous system?
final_qi.long_answer: The PNKD gene, which harbors disease-causing mutations in Paroxysmal Nonkinesigenic Dyskinesia, is transcribed into three major splice isoforms: short (PNKD-S), medium (PNKD-M) and long (PNKD-L). Transcript-profiling and protein studies consistently show that the long isoform, PNKD-L, is the one highly enriched and predominantly expressed in neurons and other cells of the central nervous system, whereas the shorter isoforms are more widely distributed in peripheral tissues. Hence, the CNS-predominant isoform is PNKD-L.
